SHOCK ORIGIN: Demand surge from a new product

Fabrication plant fire.requires: a fire in a wafer fab
Fabrication plant fire.provides: months of lost output from one site, no alternative qualified source

Export control imposed.provides: legal rather than physical unavailability, alternatives outside the controlling jurisdiction

Substrate material shortage.provides: every fab affected simultaneously, no site-specific remedy

Demand surge from a new product.provides: no supply failure at all, allocation between customers the only issue

Leading-edge logic.requires: a process node available at very few fabs
Leading-edge logic.provides: no second source in practice, years to qualify anywhere else

Mature analogue component.requires: a legacy process with many suppliers
Mature analogue component.provides: multiple qualified sources, very low unit value

Custom application-specific device.requires: a design owned by one customer
Custom application-specific device.provides: mask sets tied to one foundry, redesign required to move

Memory commodity.provides: interchangeable between suppliers, price volatility rather than availability

Qualify a second source.requires: an alternative supplier and engineering time
Qualify a second source.provides: durable resilience, six to eighteen months to achieve

Buy on the spot market.provides: immediate supply, extreme price and counterfeit risk

Redesign around available parts.provides: permanent removal of the dependency, months and recertification cost

Allocate output to priority customers.provides: continuity for some, complete cut-off for others

Product line suspended.requires: a part with no substitute at all

Feature removal to ship.requires: a redesign shipping without a function
